t:
Section 2 of the Act entitled “An Act to provide for the conveyance of a tract of land in Prince Georges County, Maryland, to the State of Maryland for use as a site for a National Guard Armory and for training the National Guard or for other military purposes”, approved August 10, 1949 (63 Stat. 592), is amended by striking out “The land” and inserting in lieu thereof “(a) Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, the land” and by adding at the end thereof the following new subsection:


“(b) 
The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development shall execute the necessary instrument or instruments to provide that a certain portion of land, not to exceed two acres, on the easterly side of the land described in the first section of this Act, as more particularly determined and designated by the Secretary of the Army, may be used for civil defense or other emergency preparedness purposes or the purposes stated in subsection (a) and that such use shall not cause the reverter clause set forth herein to become operable.”

fable.w: The section amends a land conveyance to let part of the land be used for civil defense without triggering the reverter clause, with the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development executing the instruments and the Secretary of the Army designating the portion. The tempting reading is that the State of Maryland's role as grantee makes this participation, but the State is only the recipient of the land and is not consulted before any federal decision. Every decision-maker named is a federal official, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: as more particularly determined and designated by the Secretary of the Army

qwen_block.w: This section describes an administrative action where the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development executes a land instrument based on a designation by the Secretary of the Army. Both actors are federal officials, making this intra-governmental coordination. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside party (such as the State of Maryland, local governments, or the public) before making this decision.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development shall execute the necessary instrument or instruments to provide that a certain portion of land, not to exceed two acres, on the easterly side of the land described in the first section of this Act, as more particularly determined and designated by the Secretary of the Army, may be used for civil defense or other emergency preparedness purposes

opus.w: This amendment changes the terms of a land conveyance so that part of the land can be used for civil defense without triggering the reverter clause. Only federal officials act: the HUD Secretary executes the instrument and the Secretary of the Army designates the land. Maryland is the recipient of the conveyance, but it is not consulted and has no comment, hearing, or right to object or sue. That makes it a property transaction, not outside participation in a federal decision.
opus.s: The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development shall execute the necessary instrument or instruments to provide that a certain portion of land, not to exceed two acres, on the easterly side of the land described in the first section of this Act, as more particularly determined and designated by the Secretary of the Army
opus.b: I labelled this section **No**. The tempting reading is that the State of Maryland takes part because the land was conveyed to it and an instrument has to be executed. That fails because the statute requires no consultation with, input from, or objection by the State or anyone else before the decision. Only the HUD Secretary and the Secretary of the Army act, and both are inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes an internal administrative process between two federal officials (the Secretary of HUD and the Secretary of the Army). The Secretary of the Army designates the land, and the Secretary of HUD executes the instrument. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any non-federal entities (such as state or local governments, the public, or private organizations) before making this decision. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development shall execute the necessary instrument or instruments to provide that a certain portion of land, not to exceed two acres, on the easterly side of the land described in the first section of this Act, as more particularly determined and designated by the Secretary of the Army, may be used for civil defense or other emergency preparedness purposes
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary of the Army "determines and designates" the land, and this involves a specific portion of land, there is some form of consultation or decision-making process involving outside parties. However, the text only describes an internal administrative action by federal officials (Secretary of HUD executing instruments based on Secretary of Army's designation). There is no mention of consulting with state/local governments, the public, or any non-federal entity before making this determination. The "civil defense" purpose might imply local involvement, but the statute itself does not mandate participation in the decision-making process.
